title: Saurav Das CJP: Indian government has 'lost the plot' says 'cockroach' party leader after being barred from UK flight
summary:
One of the leaders of India's "cockroach" movement has said the Delhi government has "completely lost the plot" after he was stopped from leaving the country for the UK.
In an interview with the BBC, Das said there were no discrepancies in his documents, accusing the Indian government of using cheap tactics to stop activists from travelling and speaking on issues that matter to young people.
Saurav told the BBC World Service's Newshour programme the incident showed the government was "scared".
"They are scared of the cockroach movement.
"It's a way to harass, to target activists, young voices in India by the Modi government."

title: Malaysia set to return thousands of Rohingya refugees to Myanmar
summary:
The announcement comes five days after the ICJ ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority.
Malaysia will send more than 6,500 Rohingya refugees back to Myanmar in a new round of repatriations, said Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
The UN’s highest court ruled last week that Myanmar authorities must “allow and facilitate the safe, voluntary and dignified return” of refugees displaced either within Myanmar or abroad.
Late last month, Malaysia said it would seek clarification from Myanmar about reports that hundreds of migrants recently returned to the country were being held in military detention.
The mainly Muslim Rohingya – described as the ‘world’s most persecuted minority’ – make up two-thirds of the 190,000 Myanmar refugees and asylum seekers in Malaysia, according to the United Nations.

title: Migrants using knives to slash roofs of lorries as they cross into Britain undetected - before brazenly posting about it on TikTok
summary:
Migrants are using knives to slash their way through lorries and trucks in the latest tactic to illegally sneak into Britain.
Social media footage shows male migrants brazenly showing off their blades in the back of UK-bound lorries.
Other migrants have filmed videos showing where they have slashed through roofs to sneak into lorries.
It comes after footage earlier this year showed migrants jumping from the roof of an HGV after arriving from France.
On June 26, a Malian migrant showed off a knife he used to cut a hole in a roof.

title: Danish top court’s ‘ghetto law’ ruling supports hardline immigration policy
summary:
The country’s top court said eviction of ‘non-Western’ families did not constitute discrimination.
Denmark’s top court has ruled that the eviction of “non-Western” tenants from a social housing estate under the country’s “ghetto law” was not discriminatory.
The country’s “ghetto law” housing legislation, adopted in 2018, allows for the ⁠relocation of residents from areas in which more than half of residents are “non-Western”.
It requires social housing estates to change the social mix by renting at least 60 percent of homes at market rates by 2030.
The 2018 “ghetto law” is aimed at combatting segregation and “parallel societies” in disadvantaged neighbourhoods, according to the government.
